preamble: Backing of the alveolar implosive to the velar implosive: [ɗ] becomes [ɠ]. Proto-Central Chadic had only two implosives, *ɓ and *ɗ, and Gravina (2014) treats the palatal and velar glottalized stops found in some modern languages as later innovations. In Tera, *ɗ gives ɠ in 'bone', and in Malgwa a secondary ɗʲ (itself from final *n via r) gives ɠʲ in 'three'. Gravina treats these as isolated cases, not a regular law, so certainty is low.

languageExamples.language: Proto-Central Chadic to Tera and Malgwa

examples.note: Gravina (2014: 232), example (123): *hɨkɨn > hɨkirɨ > kiɗɨ > kɨɗʲɨ > kɨɠʲɨ. The palatalized ɗʲ is the input.

sources: Gravina, R. (2014). The Phonology of Proto-Central Chadic: The Reconstruction of the Phonology and Lexicon of Proto-Central Chadic, and the Linguistic History of the Central Chadic Languages. PhD dissertation, Leiden University (LOT). https://hdl.handle.net/1887/30139
